title: Another variant of the local criterion of flatness (base change along a square of Noetherian local rings)
statement: Let $R$, $S$, $R'$, $S'$ be Noetherian local rings [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] and $\varphi:R\to S$, $\rho:R\to R'$, $\sigma:S\to S'$, $\varphi':R'\to S'$ local homomorphisms (each maps the maximal ideal into the maximal ideal) with $\sigma\circ\varphi=\varphi'\circ\rho$. Let $I\subsetneq R$ be a proper ideal and $I'=IR'$ the ideal of $R'$ generated by $\rho(I)$. Let $M$ be a finitely generated $S$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module], an $R$-module through $\varphi$, and $M'=M\otimes_SS'$, an $S'$-module through the second factor and an $R'$-module through $\varphi'$. Assume: (1) the ring map $S\otimes_RR'\to S'$, $s\otimes r'\mapsto\sigma(s)\varphi'(r')$, is a localization of $S\otimes_RR'$ at some multiplicative subset $W$ (every element of $W$ maps to a unit of $S'$; every element of $S'$ is the image of $c$ times the inverse of the image of $w$ for some $c\in S\otimes_RR'$, $w\in W$; and $c\mapsto0$ implies $wc=0$ for some $w\in W$); (2) $M/IM$ is a flat $R/I$-module [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]; (3) the homomorphism $\theta:I\otimes_RM\to I'\otimes_{R'}M'$, $a\otimes x\mapsto\rho(a)\otimes(x\otimes1)$, maps the kernel of the multiplication map $I\otimes_RM\to M$, $a\otimes x\mapsto\varphi(a)x$, to zero. Then $M'$ is a flat $R'$-module.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00MO (lemma-another-variant-local-criterion-flatness, line 23921), with hypothesis (3) on Tor_1 rewritten by Remark Tag 00M6 (remark-Tor-ring-mod-ideal, line 18690: Tor_1^R(M,R/I) = Ker(I (x)_R M -> M)), as in lem-weil-pbc-flat-variant-local-criterion (00ML); the source's proof uses Lemmas 00HI (lemma-flat-base-change), 00ML (lemma-variant-local-criterion-flatness), 00MN (lemma-surjective-on-tor-one-trivial) and 00MM (lemma-surjective-on-tor-one). The identification of the restriction of theta with the Tor map of 00MO (3) is the naturality of the isomorphism of Remark 00M6 (connecting maps of 0 -> I -> R -> R/I -> 0 and 0 -> I' -> R' -> R'/I'), which the split of this node has to write out or replace by a direct kernel argument.

proof.text: Put $A=S\otimes_RR'$ and $N=M\otimes_RR'$. The balancing relation gives an $A$-linear isomorphism $N\simeq M\otimes_SA$, $x\otimes r'\mapsto x\otimes(1\otimes r')$, with inverse $x\otimes(s\otimes r')\mapsto sx\otimes r'$. Tensoring this isomorphism over $A$ with $S'$ identifies $N\otimes_AS'$ with $M'=M\otimes_SS'$; $x\otimes r'\otimes c'\mapsto x\otimes\varphi'(r')c'$. By hypothesis (1), $A\to S'$ is a localization at $W$, so $M'$ is the localization $W^{-1}N$ as an $A$-module. If $x_1,\ldots,x_t$ generate $M$ over $S$, then $x_i\otimes1$ generate $M'$ over $S'$; hence $M'$ is finite over $S'$.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 00MO (lemma-another-variant-local-criterion-flatness, lines 23945--23947), first sentence; tensor cancellation is Algebra Tag 00D2 (lemma-tensor-with-bimodule)

proof.text: Put $Q=R/I$ and $Q'=R'/I'$. The canonical maps identify $Q\to Q'$ with the base change of $R\to R'$ to the quotient, since $Q'=R'\otimes_RQ$ as $R'$-algebras [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-quotient-base-change]. Hypothesis (2) and [lem-weil-pbc-flat-module-base-change] make $E=(M/IM)\otimes_QQ'$ flat over $Q'$. The maps $(x\bmod IM)\otimes(r'\bmod I')\mapsto(x\otimes r')\bmod I'N$ and $(x\otimes r')\bmod I'N\mapsto(x\bmod IM)\otimes(r'\bmod I')$ are inverse $Q'$-linear maps; their balancing and quotient relations follow from $I'=IR'$, so $E\simeq N/I'N$. In particular $M\otimes_RQ\simeq M/IM$ is flat over $Q$, the hypothesis needed in the next step.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 00MO (lines 23947--23950), with Lemma Tag 00HI (lemma-flat-base-change)

proof.text: Write $K=\ker(I\otimes_RM\to M)$ and $K_N=\ker(I'\otimes_{R'}N\to N)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-tor-one-surjective-flat-middle], applied to $R\to Q=R/I\to Q'=R'/I'$ and $M$ (the middle base change is $M/IM$, flat by Step 2), $\operatorname{Tor}_1^R(M,Q)\otimes_QQ'\twoheadrightarrow\operatorname{Tor}_1^R(M,Q')$. By [lem-weil-pbc-tor-ideal-kernel-naturality], $K\simeq\operatorname{Tor}_1^R(M,Q)$; this Tor group is a $Q$-module through its second variable [def-weil-pbc-tor-modules], so $I$ annihilates $K$. Thus $K\otimes_RR'\simeq K\otimes_QQ'$ by [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-over-quotient-ring]. By [lem-weil-pbc-tor-one-surjective-change-rings], with $R\to R'$ and ideal $I$, $\operatorname{Tor}_1^R(M,Q')\twoheadrightarrow\operatorname{Tor}_1^{R'}(N,Q')$. By [lem-weil-pbc-tor-ideal-kernel-naturality] the composite onto $\operatorname{Tor}_1^{R'}(N,Q')\simeq K_N$ sends $k\otimes r'$ to $r'$ times the image of $k$ under $I\otimes_RM\to I'\otimes_{R'}N$, $a\otimes x\mapsto\rho(a)\otimes(x\otimes1)$. Thus $K\otimes_RR'\twoheadrightarrow K_N$.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 00MO (lines 23953--23969), Lemma Tag 00MM (lemma-surjective-on-tor-one), Lemma Tag 00MN (lemma-surjective-on-tor-one-trivial), Remark Tag 00M6

proof.text: The map $I'\otimes_{R'}N\to N$ is $A$-linear. Localization at $W$ is exact [lem-weil-pbc-localization-module-exact], so $W^{-1}K_N$ is the kernel of its localized map. By the naturality clause of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-tensor-over-base] for the $A$-module $N$ and the $R'$-module $I'$, $W^{-1}(I'\otimes_{R'}N)\simeq I'\otimes_{R'}W^{-1}N=I'\otimes_{R'}M'$ and the localized multiplication map is $I'\otimes_{R'}M'\to M'$. Thus $K_{M'}:=\ker(I'\otimes_{R'}M'\to M')\simeq W^{-1}K_N$, and the localization of the surjection in Step 3 is onto $K_{M'}$. The image of each $k\otimes r'$ from Step 3 in $K_{M'}$ is $\varphi'(r')\theta(k)$, zero by hypothesis (3); its localization is also zero. Hence $K_{M'}=0$.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 00MO (lines 23951--23958), the localization step made explicit with Proposition Tag 00CS (proposition-localization-exact) and Lemma Tag 00DK (lemma-tensor-localization)

proof.text: The quotient $M'/I'M'$ is flat over $Q'=R'/I'$. By Step 2, $N/I'N$ is flat over $Q'$. The exact sequence $I'N\to N\to N/I'N\to0$ remains exact on localizing at $W$ [lem-weil-pbc-localization-module-exact], so $M'/I'M'\simeq W^{-1}(N/I'N)$, with $W$ acting through its image in $A/I'A$. For any injective map $U\to V$ of $Q'$-modules, flatness of $N/I'N$ makes $U\otimes_{Q'}(N/I'N)\to V\otimes_{Q'}(N/I'N)$ injective; localization at the image of $W$ in $A/I'A$ keeps it injective [lem-weil-pbc-localization-module-exact], and tensor/localization naturality [lem-weil-pbc-localization-tensor-over-base] over the base ring $Q'$ identifies it with $U\otimes_{Q'}(M'/I'M')\to V\otimes_{Q'}(M'/I'M')$. Finally $I'\subsetneq R'$ because $I\subseteq\mathfrak m_R$ and $\rho$ is local, so $I'\subseteq\mathfrak m_{R'}$. The $R'\to S'$ map is local between Noetherian local rings, $M'$ is finite over $S'$ (Step 1), its ideal-tensor multiplication is injective (Step 4), and its quotient is flat. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-variant-local-criterion] to conclude $M'$ flat over $R'$.

split_report.blueprint: The five steps realize the proof of Stacks Tag 00MO: tensor/localization identification (proof lines 23945--23947), quotient flatness and Tor-kernel surjectivity (23947--23969), localization and the final application of Tag 00ML (23951--23969).
split_report.summary: Split Stacks Algebra 00MO through its two Tor-surjectivity lemmas 00MM and 00MN and the naturality of the Tor-to-ideal-kernel identification 00M6. Tensor cancellation identifies the module after the square's base change with a localization; the quotient is flat by 00HI and localization exactness. The Tor surjections make the original ideal-tensor kernel surject onto the kernel before localization; hypothesis (3) kills the localized kernel, and 00ML yields flatness. The three missing source lemmas are new unsplit nodes; no Mathlib match was found in the searches recorded there.
